{{Short description|British mathematician and theoretical physicist}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=February 2018}}
{{Use British English|date=February 2018}}
'''David B. Fairlie''' (born in South Queensferry, Scotland, 1935) is a British [[mathematician]] and  [[theoretical physicist]], Professor Emeritus at the
[[University of Durham]] (UK).<ref>[https://www.dur.ac.uk/research/directory/staff/?mode=staff&id=458  Prof Fairlie's University of Durham web-page]</ref>

He was educated in mathematical physics at the [[University of Edinburgh]] (BSc 1957),
and  he earned a PhD at the [[University of Cambridge]] in 1960, under the 
supervision of [[John Polkinghorne]]. After postdoctoral training at [[Princeton University]]
and Cambridge, he was lecturer in [[University of St Andrews|St. Andrews]] (1962–64) and at Durham University 
(1964), retiring as Professor (2000). 
 
He has made numerous influential contributions<ref>Prof Fairlie's  physics publications are available on the INSPIRE Database [http://inspirehep.net/search?ln=en&ln=en&p=a+d+b+fairlie+and+topcite+40%2B&of=hb&action_search=Search&sf=&so=d&rm=&rg=25&sc=0] and the GoogleCite database [https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=D+B+Fairlie&btnG=&hl=en&as_sdt=0%2C14].</ref> in [[particle physics|particle]] and mathematical [[physics]], 
notably in the early formulation of [[string theory]],<ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Fairlie | first1 = D. B. | last2 = Nielsen | first2 = H. B. | doi = 10.1016/0550-3213(70)90393-7 | title = An analogue model for KSV theory | journal = Nuclear Physics B | volume = 20 | issue = 3 | pages = 637 | year = 1970 |bibcode = 1970NuPhB..20..637F }}; {{Cite journal | last1 = Corrigan | first1 = E. | last2 = Fairlie | first2 = D. B. | doi = 10.1016/0550-3213(75)90125-X | title = Off-shell states in dual resonance theory | journal = Nuclear Physics B | volume = 91 | issue = 3 | pages = 527 | year = 1975 |bibcode = 1975NuPhB..91..527C | url = https://cds.cern.ch/record/873246/files/CM-P00060609.pdf }}</ref> as well as the determination of the [[Weinberg angle|weak mixing angle]] in [[Extra dimensions#Additional dimensions|extra dimensions]],<ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Fairlie | first1 = D. B. | doi = 10.1016/0370-2693(79)90434-9 | title = Higgs fields and the determination of the Weinberg angle | journal = Physics Letters B | volume = 82 | pages = 97–100 | year = 1979 | issue = 1 |bibcode = 1979PhLB...82...97F }}</ref> infinite-dimensional [[Lie algebra]]s,<ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Fairlie | first1 = D. B. | last2 = Fletcher | first2 = P. | last3 = Zachos | first3 = C. K. | doi = 10.1016/0370-2693(89)91418-4 | title = Trigonometric structure constants for new infinite-dimensional algebras | journal = Physics Letters B | volume = 218 | issue = 2 | pages = 203 | year = 1989 |bibcode = 1989PhLB..218..203F }}</ref> classical solutions of [[gauge theories]],
<ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Corrigan | first1 = E. | last2 = Fairlie | first2 = D. B. | doi = 10.1016/0370-2693(77)90808-5 | title = Scalar field theory and exact solutions to a classical SU (2) gauge theory | journal = Physics Letters B | volume = 67 | pages = 69–71 | year = 1977 | issue = 1 |bibcode = 1977PhLB...67...69C }}</ref> higher-dimensional 
gauge theories,<ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Corrigan | first1 = E. | last2 = Devchand | first2 = C. | last3 = Fairlie | first3 = D. B. | last4 = Nuyts | first4 = J. | title = First-order equations for gauge fields in spaces of dimension greater than four | doi = 10.1016/0550-3213(83)90244-4 | journal = Nuclear Physics B | volume = 214 | issue = 3 | pages = 452 | year = 1983 |bibcode = 1983NuPhB.214..452C }}</ref> and 
[[phase space formulation|deformation quantization]].<ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Fairlie | first1 = D. B. | title = The formulation of quantum mechanics in terms of phase space functions | doi = 10.1017/S0305004100038068 | journal = [[Mathematical Proceedings of the Cambridge Philosophical Society]] | volume = 60 | issue = 3 | pages = 581–586 | year = 1964|bibcode = 1964PCPS...60..581F }}</ref>  
 
He has co-authored several volumes, notably<ref>[[Cosmas Zachos|Cosmas K. Zachos]], David B. Fairlie, and [[Thomas Curtright|Thomas L. Curtright]], ''[[Quantum Mechanics]] in Phase Space'',  (World Scientific,  Singapore, 2005) {{ISBN|978-981-238-384-6}}  
[http://www.worldscibooks.com/physics/5287.html].</ref><ref>Thomas L Curtright, David B Fairlie, Cosmas K Zachos, ''A Concise Treatise on Quantum Mechanics in Phase Space'',  (World Scientific,  Singapore, 2014)  {{ISBN|9789814520430}}</ref> on [[quantum mechanics]] in [[phase space]].
